pairs.why: A's paper edge is crisp with thin precise fold seams, like the real map's clean white border, while B's rim is rounder and softer.
A has thin precise seams and lime piping lines like the real pack, while B's puffy clay edges and prominent rivets are softer and blobbier.
A has thin, crisp panel seams and clean hard silhouette edges like the real cards, while B has thicker, softer rounded contours.
A has the real cooler's crisp, chunky outer edge and clean white-on-red boundaries, while B's softer edges and blurred background lose that definition.
Both drums have similar crisp gold rims and tubular stands, so edges give no reason to prefer either.
A has bold stone edges and a firm table contour, close to the real table's chunky bevels and cracks, while B's thin, tiny lines read weaker.
B's smooth rope has few interior lines like the real cards' clean forms, while A's dense twist grooves add too many internal edges.
A's truss is softer and less dense and its lamp edges are soft, like the real card, while B's truss is a busy, hard-edged cluster of lines.
